title: Differentially Private Spectral Monitor Logs for Hallucination Detection: A Comparative Study of Wishart and Gaussian Mechanisms

contributions.purpose: Determine the correct DP mechanism for privatizing EigenScore-style hidden-state covariance matrices.
contributions.mechanism: Comparative study of the Wishart mechanism (PSD-preserving) versus the standard Gaussian mechanism (which needs destructive PSD projection) on OPT-6.7B with SQuAD v2.0.
contributions.evaluation: Wishart strictly dominates Gaussian, achieving 55.1% vs 50.7% AUROC (+4.4pp) at epsilon=1 by avoiding PSD projection that clamps ~half the eigenvalues to zero.
contributions.domain: differential privacy for spectral hallucination monitoring
contributions.source_quote: We show the Wishart mechanism strictly dominates Gaussian DP for covariance privatization, achieving +4.4pp higher AUROC at epsilon=1 by avoiding destructive PSD projection.

contributions.purpose: Assess the actual privacy threat to EigenScore monitor logs.
contributions.mechanism: Run a canary-ID attack on EigenScore covariance logs without any DP protection.
contributions.evaluation: Near-chance leakage: 0.74% canary-ID accuracy vs 0.50% chance, suggesting a weaker threat model than anticipated.
contributions.source_quote: We find that EigenScore logs exhibit minimal privacy leakage even without DP (0.74% vs 0.50% chance), suggesting a weaker threat model than anticipated.

contributions.purpose: Explain why DP-protected spectral monitoring cannot reach acceptable utility.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze signal-to-noise ratio of K=10 covariance signal eigenvalues against injected DP noise.
contributions.evaluation: SNR limitation: K=10 signal eigenvalues (~0.6) are easily overwhelmed by DP noise, preventing acceptable utility at reasonable privacy budgets (epsilon<=10).
contributions.source_quote: We identify fundamental SNR limitations: K=10 covariance signal eigenvalues (~0.6) are easily overwhelmed by DP noise, preventing acceptable utility at reasonable privacy budgets.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We present the first comparative study of Wishart (Jiang et al., 2015) versus Gaussian mechanisms for privatizing EigenScore-style covariance statistics.
The Wishart mechanism (Jiang et al., 2015) addresses this limitation by sampling noise from a Wishart distribution, producing PSD matrices by construction while providing pure (epsilon, 0)-DP.

INSIDE (Chen et al., 2024) introduced EigenScore, which uses covariance eigenvalues from stochastic generations as an uncertainty proxy... Our work focuses on privatizing the spectral statistics produced by EigenScore-style methods.
EigenScore (Chen et al., 2024) quantifies hallucination likelihood by measuring semantic divergence across multiple stochastic generations.

notes: MIXED/NEGATIVE-RESULT paper: positive comparative finding (Wishart dominates Gaussian, +4.4pp) but overall negative conclusion (SNR limits prevent acceptable utility at epsilon<=10) plus a near-tie/near-chance leakage result (0.74% vs 0.50% chance) implying a weaker-than-expected threat. Adapts existing Wishart mechanism (Jiang et al. 2015) and EigenScore (Chen et al. 2024). Strongly overlaps in topic with FA0187.
